rationale: Start with a broad, mid-length scouting gradient to elute all 10 compounds if possible and reveal the overall retention window and any strongly retained species. A moderate temperature helps keep run time reasonable without being so aggressive that it obscures selectivity trends for later optimization.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to reduce t_last and improve the time term. Keep the same wide gradient window and temperature, and shorten tG one step to see how much run time can be cut before any pair approaches the 1.5 resolution threshold.

The current method is very close to the 10 min target and the worst pair is still above the 1.5 cutoff, so one more reduction in gradient time is the most direct way to test whether a perfect or near-perfect CRF is reachable. Holding phi0, phi1, and T constant isolates the effect of slope on the critical pair.

At 14 min the run is fast enough, so the next move is to recover resolution for the 6/7 critical pair without lengthening the gradient. Lowering temperature often increases selectivity and may push that pair back above 1.5 while keeping t_last near 10 min.

Lowering T hurt selectivity badly, so test the opposite direction at the same fast 14 min gradient. A modest increase to 45 C may improve the critical mid-cluster selectivity enough to restore full resolution while keeping the last peak under 10 min.

Temperature changes worsened the crowded middle cluster, so keep T at 40 C and instead make the initial gradient composition slightly stronger to reshape early/mid selectivity at the same fast run time. This could relieve the critical overlap around peaks 5–7 while preserving t_last below 10 min.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved both t_last and the critical 6/7 pair, so continue in the same direction to probe for a selectivity maximum. This keeps the run fast while testing whether a slightly steeper start can push the last sub-1.5 pair over the threshold.

The best run so far is at phi0 0.10, and increasing phi0 further did not help the critical pair, so now narrow the gradient window from the strong end. Lowering phi1 slightly can reduce compression late in the gradient and may improve the 6/7 selectivity without sacrificing the already acceptable last peak time.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical 6/7 pair substantially while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This tests whether a slightly narrower gradient window can lift the last pair above R = 1.5 and reach the maximum CRF.

Now that all pairs are resolved at the threshold, the only possible improvement is to keep full resolution while shortening the method. Reducing tG by one step with the same successful composition window is the cleanest test for a faster still-perfect method.

Shortening tG lost resolution on the same critical pair, so revert to 14 min and continue testing whether a slightly lower phi1 can preserve or improve full resolution. This may create a bit more selectivity margin for peaks 6/7, even if t_last moves slightly above 10 min.

The current optimum is already perfect, so the only useful remaining search is for an equally resolved but faster variant. At 14 min and phi1 0.85, try a higher temperature to pull t_last below 10 min while checking whether the 6/7 pair can stay at or above the 1.5 threshold.

High temperature collapsed the critical pair, so test the opposite side of the optimum with the otherwise perfect method. If 35 C preserves full resolution and only slightly increases retention, it could reveal whether 40 C is truly the selectivity sweet spot around the 10 min boundary.

The optimum is clearly centered at 40 C, so explore composition around the winning phi1 = 0.85 by lowering phi0 one step from the best method. This checks whether a weaker starting composition can further improve the crowded 5–7 region while retaining full resolution near the 10 min limit.

The best method is already perfect, but to map the local optimum completely, test the other side of phi0 at the same successful phi1 and tG. This will show whether phi0 = 0.10 is a true optimum or whether a stronger start can keep full resolution with a shorter elution window.

Phi0 = 0.15, phi1 = 0.85, tG = 14, T = 40 has reached CRF 1.000 with a slightly shorter last peak time than the earlier optimum, so continue one more step in phi0 to see if the method can stay fully resolved while moving even earlier. This is a targeted local refinement around the current best region.

Phi0 = 0.15 and phi1 = 0.85 gave a perfect score with slightly better timing than the earlier optimum, so the next logical refinement is to lower phi1 one step at that phi0. This tests whether added selectivity from a narrower window can be retained while keeping the last peak under 10 min.

With phi0 fixed at 0.15, lowering phi1 to 0.80 increased resolution margin but pushed t_last above 10 min, so test the other side at phi1 0.90. This will bracket the local optimum and determine whether phi1 = 0.85 is indeed the best balance of full resolution and speed.

Two methods already achieve CRF 1.000, and phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85 is the faster of them; now probe whether a slightly longer gradient can add resolution margin without a time penalty. If t_last stays under 10 min, this could reveal a more robust perfect method around the same optimum.

The remaining useful search is along the fast edge of the perfect region: phi0 = 0.20, phi1 = 0.85 was fast but under-resolved, while lowering phi1 generally improves the critical pair. Testing phi0 0.20 with phi1 0.80 may recover full resolution while keeping t_last safely below 10 min.

The new perfect method at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.80 suggests the optimum ridge may continue toward higher phi0 and lower phi1 while keeping the run fast. One more step to phi0 0.25 tests the edge of that region and may still preserve full resolution with an even earlier elution profile.

Phi0 = 0.25 is too aggressive and causes early coelution, so stay at the perfect phi0 = 0.20 and lower phi1 one more step to probe the lower-phi1 boundary. This tests whether the perfect region extends to an even narrower window while keeping the fast elution profile.

Phi0 = 0.20, phi1 = 0.80 is now a perfect method, so the remaining chance to improve robustness-speed tradeoff is to shorten tG one step at this composition. This checks whether the stronger, narrower window at higher phi0 can tolerate a 12 min gradient better than the earlier phi0 0.10 case.

With only two injections left and multiple perfect methods already found, use the remaining budget to map the upper phi1 boundary at the phi0 = 0.20 optimum region. This checks whether phi0 0.20 can support a broader gradient window while retaining full resolution and may clarify the shape of the perfect-method ridge.

Two perfect methods are known at 14 min, so for the final injection test whether the more robust phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85 composition can support a shorter 12 min gradient better than the phi0 0.20 or phi0 0.10 variants. This is the last meaningful chance to find a faster fully resolved method.
